newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey coalition halts Islamist castle plans.
newsitem.headline: Turkey coalition halts Islamist castle plans.

text.p: Turkey's secularist government has delayed plans to restore a mosque in a 15th century Crusader castle in one of its first acts in office, a culture ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
He said new Culture Minister Istemihan Talay had halted an attempt begun by his Islamist predecessor to move an archaelogical museum out of a disused mosque in Bodrum Castle.
"The order to move the exhibition has been stopped temporarily while the minister looks into the matter," the spokesman told Reuters.
He said the previous minister had planned to emphasise the "religious identity" of the mosque, originally a Christian chapel, but that restoring it as a place of worship had not been proposed.
A secularist coalition took power on Monday to replace the government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who resigned last month after frequent rows over Islamist activism.

Around 1,500 people had protested in Bodrum, a popular seaside resort famed for its nightclubs, against the ministry's plan to move the underwater archeology museum, which houses an ancient ship wreckage.
